free_tier.stated: Explicit, from their own page: 'No, we have no storage or bandwidth limits. We only have a 5GB per file limit.' Help centre repeats: 'Payhip supports a maximum file size of 5GB per digital product.'

per_object_cap.stated: maximum file size of 5GB per digital product
per_object_cap.notes: Each uploaded file can be up to 5GB in size; larger files can be split into multiple smaller files uploaded to the same product listing.

egress.terms: No, we have no storage or bandwidth limits. We only have a 5GB per file limit.

record.interface_detail: Web upload. REST API + webhooks on paid plans; the digital-product upload itself is form-based.
record.chaining: Each uploaded file can be up to 5GB; larger files can be split into multiple smaller files and uploaded separately to the same product listing.
record.limits_note: Per-object-cap 5 GB. The only limit they publish. Extension blocklist is a hard gate on ingress: EXE, ISO, DMG, VBS, SCR refused unless inside a ZIP. No aggregate quota.

identity_cost.detail: a first name, last name, email address and password on the free-account form. No card is asked for: the help centre adds card details only to upgrade a paid plan. No phone field is on the form.

record.reliability_note: Serving path is fine; the operational risk is that a 'digital product' must be a listed product, and free products still sit behind a checkout page. Buyer link is emailed, not a stable public URL. So it is an archive/delivery tier, not a hot-link CDN.
